summary: A switch — a checkbox with role="switch", announced as on/off.
useWhen: the change takes effect immediately: a setting, a feature flag, a preference

useInstead.when: the value is collected and submitted with a form
useInstead.why: a switch reads as taking effect now; a checkbox reads as a value being gathered

useInstead.when: there are more than two states

sm.use: dense settings rows and table filters

lg.use: touch targets and prominent single settings

neutral.use: a setting with no positive or negative reading — display and layout preferences

danger.use: turning on something destructive or hard to undo

children.note: the visible label; omit for a bare switch and supply `aria-label`

guarantees: a real <input type="checkbox"> underneath, so form association, label clicking and `:checked` come from the platform
`role="switch"` changes only the announcement — "on/off" rather than "checked/unchecked"
requires: `children`, or `aria-label` when there is no visible label

antiPatterns.dont: a Toggle with a Save button beside it
antiPatterns.why: a switch says the change is already applied; if it needs saving it is a Checkbox

antiPatterns.dont: labelling a Toggle "Enable dark mode?" as a question
antiPatterns.why: a switch label names the thing being switched, not a question about it

antiPatterns.dont: a button with `aria-pressed` for a setting
antiPatterns.why: a switch is a form value; the checkbox gives form association and `:checked` for free
